page: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine configured with 128 vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations. Local storage is bundled, providing 7559 GB of local disk capacity alongside Premium Storage compatibility.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 144,593.74 and a PassMark CPU score of 132,394.2. Memory subsystem performance is highly efficient, achieving uncached read bandwidths of 655.3 GB/sec and write bandwidths of 253.51 GB/sec. Database operations are highly performant, as evidenced by a PassMark database score of 33,918.49 and a Redis SET throughput of 209.67 million operations per second. Single-core performance sits in the average tier, indicating that the server's strength lies in highly parallelized workloads.

Given its high memory density, massive local storage, and strong multi-threaded performance, the E128ds_v7 is optimized for memory-intensive enterprise applications, large-scale relational databases, and in-memory caching layers. The inclusion of Intel AMX instructions also supports CPU-based machine learning inference, where it demonstrates strong prompt processing speeds, though text generation speeds remain average. The lack of dedicated GPU hardware makes it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, but it represents a highly resource-dense option for data-heavy enterprise workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family virtual machine designed for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It features 128 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 64 physical cores, 1024.0 GB of RAM, and 7559 GB of local storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and outstanding database execution speeds, including a Redis throughput of 209.67 million operations per second. While single-core performance is average, its massive parallel processing capacity and high memory density make it highly cost-efficient for large-scale enterprise databases, in-memory analytics, and parallelized data processing pipelines.
